Major US bank outages hit customers

7.text: JPMorgan is only mentioned as one of the big banks kicking off Q4 2026 earnings on January 14. The other articles cover Bank of America, Goldman Sachs, Wells Fargo, Citigroup, and general bank-sector news.

10.text: Dividend and financial-sector articles highlight income strategies for retirees, with banks favored if the Fed hikes rates again. JPMorgan is only tangentially relevant, mentioned as a possible holding in diversified dividend portfolios.

4.text: JPMorgan and Hyundai Card are piloting AI agents that execute business payments without direct human intervention via Kinexys. JPMorgan also disclosed a cyberattack at an outside vendor, is building a Dallas fund-banking hub, and named Bregje de Best to succeed CFO Jeremy Barnum after Q1 2027.

12.text: JPMorgan named Bregje de Best as firmwide CFO effective after Q1 2027, succeeding Jeremy Barnum, who becomes vice chairman. The stock fell 1.77% to $324.11, with analysts expecting Q3 EPS of $5.94 and revenue of $50.95 billion.

17.text: JPMorgan Chase resolved a software bug that disrupted online banking, balances, and transfers for US customers, ruling out a cyberattack. Separately, the bank disclosed a vendor cyberattack that may have exposed customer names and emails, unrelated to the outage.

5.text: JPMorgan raised Disney's target to $140, cut iQIYI's to $1.20 and Home Depot's to $390, and lifted Moderna's while still calling it overvalued. It also downgraded Scout24 to neutral on AI search risk, sending shares down 6%.

13.text: JPMorgan isn't named in these articles; they cover Wall Street banks' Bitcoin ETF holdings before a crash, a Hong Kong–Swift blockchain payments test, and a Chase outage cited as showing Bitcoin's resilience.

16.text: iRhythm signed a $100 million accelerated share repurchase agreement. JPMorgan is likely the counterparty bank, though the article excerpt does not name it.

18.text: JPMorgan is mentioned only as a sponsor/host context for CorpGov's sixth Palm Beach CorpGov Forum (Nov 4–5, 2026), which focused on executing as a public company after an IPO.
